content: Zerit® is the brand name for stavudine (d4T), which is a synthetic thymidine nucleoside analogue with activity against human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1). The chemical name of stavudine is 2′,3′-didehydro-3′-deoxythymidine. At a temperature of 23°C, stavudine has a solubility of approximately 83 mg/mL in water and 30 mg/mL in propylene glycol. Zerit is available in capsule form for oral administration, with each capsule containing either 15 mg, 20 mg, 30 mg, or 40 mg of stavudine. The capsules also include the following inactive ingredients: microcrystalline cellulose, sodium starch glycolate, lactose, and magnesium stearate. The hard gelatin shell of the capsules is composed of gelatin, titanium dioxide, and iron oxides. The capsules are printed with edible inks. Zerit is also available as a dye-free, fruit-flavored powder for oral solution. When reconstituted with water according to the label instructions, the powder provides 200 mL of a 1 mg/mL stavudine oral solution. The powder formulation contains the following inactive ingredients: methylparaben, propylparaben, sodium carboxymethylcellulose, sucrose, and agents for antifoaming and flavoring. The bottles are equipped with child-resistant closures.
